subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: detects physiological signals such as heart rate, muscle activity, temperature and motion.

subsystems.name: Conductive network
subsystems.role: carries electrical signals from sensors to the processing unit without bulky wires.

subsystems.name: Textile substrate
subsystems.role: hosts the electronics while remaining comfortable, breathable and stretchable.

subsystems.name: Electronics module
subsystems.role: processes sensor data and transmits it wirelessly.

subsystems.name: Encapsulation
subsystems.role: protects the electronics and graphene from sweat and repeated washing.

buildSteps.title: Produce graphene
buildSteps.detail: Graphene is made by chemical vapour deposition on metal foil, by reducing graphene oxide, or by liquid-phase exfoliation to create a printable ink.

buildSteps.title: Formulate ink or coating
buildSteps.detail: Graphene is dispersed in a solvent with binders and surfactants to make a stable ink or sprayable coating.

buildSteps.title: Apply to textile
buildSteps.detail: The ink is screen-printed, dip-coated or sprayed onto fabric, or mixed into polymer and spun into fibres.

buildSteps.title: Pattern sensors and interconnects
buildSteps.detail: Masks or direct printing create specific sensor shapes and conductive paths that connect them.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: A microcontroller, flexible battery and wireless module are attached using conductive adhesives or stitching.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: A waterproof, stretchable polymer is applied to protect the active layers from moisture and mechanical wear.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Sensor response is measured against reference instruments, and the garment is washed and stretched to check durability.

buildSteps.title: Assemble garment
buildSteps.detail: The functional fabric is cut and sewn into the final clothing item, with connectors for charging and data.

prerequisites.why: methods exist but cost, uniformity and volume must improve for mass-market textiles.
some flexible batteries exist, but energy density and survival through washing cycles remain limited.
conductive yarns and coatings are used in niche products, but graphene integration is still being refined.
Bluetooth Low Energy and similar protocols can transmit data, though medical-grade security and privacy need attention.
some wearable sensors are cleared for clinical use, but graphene-based garments require new validation.

pathway.milestone: laboratory prototypes and early commercial products with basic motion or heart-rate sensing
pathway.unlocks: proof that graphene can survive textile processing and daily wear.

pathway.milestone: pilot production for fitness and remote patient monitoring
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on comfort, washability and sensor accuracy.

pathway.milestone: commercial launch of medical-grade graphene clothing for continuous vital-sign monitoring
pathway.unlocks: shift from hospital-based to home-based monitoring for chronic conditions.

pathway.milestone: mainstream adoption with integrated energy harvesting and closed-loop health feedback
pathway.unlocks: personalised preventive healthcare and new fashion-tech applications.
